source.section: 2. A simultaneous-zero lemma (base b), with setup from section 1

target_statement: For every integer base b>=2, a consecutive interval of at least two simultaneous zero digits in forward and old-width-reflected ordinary carry equations has either every old coefficient zero or every old coefficient b-1. Prove a generic binary-carry equation lemma, the actual unchanged ordinary normalization specialization, and a canonical positive-digit specialization with the original numeric reverse-add bridge.

hypotheses.generic: q,a,c,r,u : Nat -> Int; 2<=b; 2<=k; q nonnegative on [s,s+k); a,c each in {0,1} on the closed boundary interval [s,s+k]; q_i+a_i=r_i+b*a_(i+1); q_i+c_(i+1)=u_i+b*c_i; r_i=u_i=0 throughout [s,s+k).
hypotheses.actual: ResetNormalization.Bounded b xs; (xs.map Prod.fst).reverse=xs.map Prod.fst; s+k<=xs.length; both actual body digits at i and xs.length-1-i zero. No terminal-carry or no-overflow premise.
hypotheses.canonical: Existing ReverseAdd.DigitBounds, PhysicalWidth.PositiveLast and xs.map Prod.fst=ReverseAdd.pairs digits instantiate the actual theorem, retaining original reverse_add_normalization value/width facts.

conclusion: A single disjunction for the whole interval: (forall i in [s,s+k), q_i=0) OR (forall i in [s,s+k), q_i=b-1). Not just a pointwise disjunction.
boundaries: k>=2 essential; length one has counterexamples
Carry constraints include both boundary indices
Reflected output uses old-width body even on overflow
Ordinary tags erase reset flags using existing semantics
